examples.ko: 회의 전에 계획서를 먼저 읽어 주세요.
examples.en: Please read the plan first before the meeting.

examples.ko: 이 계획서는 너무 길어서 다시 써야 해요.
examples.en: This plan is too long, so I have to rewrite it.
Do you know where my plan is?

examples.ko: 이 계획서로 다음 주부터 일을 시작해요.
examples.en: We start the work next week based on this plan.

examples.ko: 사업 계획서에 필요한 돈도 꼭 적어야 해요.
examples.en: You must also write the money needed in the business plan.
You even made a travel plan document. You are so thorough!

explain: 계획은 머릿속 생각이고, 계획서는 그 생각을 종이나 파일에 적은 문서예요. '계획서를 쓰다', '계획서를 내다'처럼 문서를 다루는 동사와 같이 써요. 한 일을 알리는 문서는 '보고서'라고 해요.
explain_en: '계획' is the idea in your head, and 계획서 is that idea written down in a document. It goes with verbs for handling documents, such as '계획서를 쓰다' (write) and '계획서를 내다' (submit). A document that reports what was already done is a '보고서'.

examples.en: The children are amazed when they see the magic trick.
Everyone was amazed at his singing skills.
My parents were amazed at my Korean skills too.

examples.ko: 선물을 받고 놀라워하는 친구의 얼굴이 기억나요.
examples.en: I remember my friend's amazed face when she got the gift.

examples.ko: 사람들은 새 건물을 보고 놀라워하고 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: People were amazed at the new building and took pictures.
Your teacher will be amazed when she hears the result.

explain: '놀랍다'는 내가 느끼는 마음이고, '놀라워하다'는 그렇게 느끼는 모습을 겉으로 보이는 거예요. 그래서 '친구가 놀라워해요'처럼 다른 사람 이야기에 잘 어울려요. 갑자기 깜짝 하는 것은 '놀라다'라고 해요.
explain_en: '놀랍다' is the feeling you have inside, while 놀라워하다 shows that feeling on the outside. That is why it fits well with another person's reaction, like '친구가 놀라워해요'. A sudden jump of surprise is '놀라다'.

examples.en: I turned the radio dial and made the sound louder.

examples.ko: 다이얼이 고장 나서 문이 안 열려요.
examples.en: The dial is broken, so the door will not open.
Old phones used a dial to enter the number.
Please turn the oven dial to the right.

examples.ko: 할아버지 집에는 다이얼 전화기가 아직 있어요.
examples.en: My grandfather's house still has a dial phone.

examples.ko: 작은 다이얼도 하나 있고 버튼도 두 개 있어요.
examples.en: There is one small dial and two buttons too.

explain: '다이얼을 돌리다'처럼 돌리는 동작과 같이 써요. 버튼은 누르고 다이얼은 돌려요. 전화를 걸 때는 보통 '전화를 걸다'라고 하고, 다이얼은 옛날 돌리는 전화기를 이야기할 때 나와요.
explain_en: It goes with the action of turning, as in '다이얼을 돌리다'. You press a '버튼' but you turn a 다이얼. To make a phone call people normally say '전화를 걸다', and 다이얼 comes up when talking about old rotary phones.

examples.en: Our cat is a calico, with three colors.
This cloth is woven in three colors.
I made a bracelet with three-colored thread.

examples.ko: 빨강, 노랑, 파랑 삼색을 섞어 그림을 그려요.
examples.en: I mix the three colors red, yellow and blue to paint.
A three-colored flag is waving in the wind.
I bought clothes where the three colors go well together.

explain: 고양이 털 색이 세 가지면 '삼색 고양이'라고 해요. '삼색 실', '삼색 볼펜'처럼 뒤에 오는 명사 앞에 붙여 써요. 색 세 개를 풀어서 말할 때는 '세 가지 색'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: A cat whose fur has three colors is called a '삼색 고양이'. You can put it before another noun, as in '삼색 실' or '삼색 볼펜'. When you spell it out, you can also say '세 가지 색'.

examples.ko: 헌 가방 말고 새것을 사고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to buy a new one, not an old bag.
These shoes are clean, like new.
A new one is expensive, so I bought a used one.
I threw away the worn cup and replaced it with a new one.
If you need a new one, go to the shop and ask.

examples.ko: 이 책은 아직 새것이라서 아껴서 읽어요.
examples.en: This book is still new, so I read it carefully.

explain: '새 옷', '새 가방'처럼 물건 이름을 같이 말하면 '새'를 써요. 이미 말한 물건을 다시 가리킬 때는 '새것'이라고 해요. 반대는 '헌것'이나 '낡은 것'이에요.
explain_en: When you name the item, you use '새' as in '새 옷' and '새 가방'. When you point back to an item you already mentioned, you say 새것. The opposite is '헌것' or '낡은 것'.

en: be taken away; be arrested and taken away

examples.en: The thief was caught and taken away by the police.

examples.ko: 아이가 낯선 사람에게 잡혀가는 꿈을 꿨어요.
examples.en: I had a dream that a child was taken away by a stranger.
In old tales, the bad people get taken away.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 왜 잡혀갔는지 아무도 몰라요.
examples.en: Nobody knows why that person was taken away.
If you do wrong, you could be taken to the police station.
After the criminal was taken away, the town became quiet.

explain: '잡다'에 피동을 만드는 '-히-'가 붙은 '잡히다'와 '가다'가 합쳐진 말이에요. 잡는 쪽이 주어면 '경찰이 도둑을 잡아가요', 잡힌 사람이 주어면 '도둑이 경찰에게 잡혀가요'라고 해요. 잡는 사람 뒤에는 '에게'나 '한테'를 붙여요.
explain_en: It combines '잡히다' (the passive of '잡다') with '가다'. If the catcher is the subject you say '경찰이 도둑을 잡아가요', and if the caught person is the subject you say '도둑이 경찰에게 잡혀가요'. The person who catches gets '에게' or '한테'.

examples.ko: 큰길 위에 새 영화 광고판이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: A billboard for a new movie was put up over the main road.

examples.ko: 버스 정류장 광고판을 보고 가수 이름을 알았어요.
examples.en: I learned the singer's name from the ad board at the bus stop.

examples.ko: 광고판에는 신제품 사진이 크게 나와 있어요.
examples.en: The billboard shows a big picture of the new product.

examples.ko: 비가 와서 광고판의 불빛이 흐리게 보여요.
examples.en: Because of the rain, the light of the billboard looks blurry.
I decided to meet my friend in front of the billboard.
I heard the old billboard will be replaced with a new one tomorrow.

explain: '간판'은 가게가 자기 이름을 걸어 두는 판이고, 광고판은 광고를 보여 주는 판이에요. 불빛이 나오는 화면으로 된 것은 '전광판'이라고 해요. 길가나 건물 위에서 볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: A '간판' is the sign a shop hangs with its own name, while 광고판 shows advertisements. One made of a lit-up screen is called a '전광판'. You can see them by the road or on top of buildings.

examples.en: I wear comfortable leggings when I exercise.
These leggings stretch well, so they are comfortable.
The leggings were small, so I changed them to a bigger size.
I wore a long T-shirt over black leggings.

examples.ko: 동생이 새 레깅스도 사고 양말도 샀어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling bought new leggings and socks too.
I came to yoga class after changing into leggings.

explain: 바지처럼 '입다'와 같이 써요. 영어 leggings처럼 s가 붙은 모양이지만 한국어는 복수 표시가 따로 없어서 하나든 여러 개든 '레깅스'예요. 헐렁한 '바지'와 달리 몸에 붙는 옷을 말할 때 써요.
explain_en: Like '바지', it goes with the verb '입다'. It looks plural in English, but Korean has no plural marker, so 레깅스 is used for one pair or many. You use it for a close-fitting garment, unlike a loose '바지'.

examples.en: The wind blew and my hair got all messed up.

examples.ko: 빗에 붙은 머리털을 하나씩 떼어 냈어요.
examples.en: I took the hairs stuck on the comb off one by one.
A baby's hair is very soft.
There is a lot of dust on your hair.
Even my hair got soaked, so I dried it with a towel.
My older brother has a lot of hair and is tall too.

explain: '머리카락'과 같은 뜻으로 쓰지만, 한 올씩 셀 때는 '머리카락 한 올'이라고 해요. 말할 때는 그냥 '머리'라고도 해서 '머리가 길어요'처럼 말해요. 머리 위의 털 전체를 말하는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It can be used like '머리카락', but when counting single strands you say '머리카락 한 올'. In speech people often just say '머리', as in '머리가 길어요'. 머리털 has the feel of all the hair on the head.

examples.ko: 그 가게 직원은 너무 불친절해서 다시 가기 싫어요.
examples.en: The staff at that shop were so unfriendly that I do not want to go again.

examples.ko: 불친절한 택시 기사를 만나서 기분이 나빴어요.
examples.en: I met an unfriendly taxi driver and felt bad.
The restaurant owner was unfriendly to the customers.
If the staff are unfriendly, customers will decrease.

examples.ko: 이 호텔은 사진은 예쁜데 서비스가 불친절해요.
examples.en: The photos of this hotel are pretty, but the service is unfriendly.

examples.ko: 불친절하다는 이야기를 듣고 후기를 다시 읽어 봤어요.
examples.en: I heard it was unfriendly, so I read the reviews again.

explain: '친절하다'의 반대말이고, '불-'은 '불가능', '불행'처럼 반대를 만들어요. 가게 직원이나 서비스의 태도를 말할 때 어울려요. 성격이 정이 없어 보이는 사람은 '무뚝뚝하다'고 해요.
explain_en: It is the opposite of '친절하다', and '불-' makes opposites as in '불가능' and '불행'. It fits the attitude of shop staff or a service. A person who seems cold by nature is called '무뚝뚝하다'.

examples.en: I met a friend who works at a magazine company.

examples.ko: 저는 대학 졸업 후 잡지사에 들어갔어요.
examples.en: After graduating from university, I joined a magazine company.

examples.ko: 이 잡지사는 매달 새 책을 내요.
examples.en: This magazine company puts out a new issue every month.

examples.ko: 잡지사가 제 사진을 쓰고 싶다고 연락했어요.
examples.en: A magazine company contacted me and said they want to use my photo.
A reporter from a big magazine company came to the school.
I mailed the letter for the magazine company at the post office.

explain: '-사'는 회사를 뜻해서 신문을 만드는 곳은 '신문사', 책을 만드는 곳은 '출판사'라고 해요. 잡지를 만드는 회사는 잡지사예요. '잡지사에 다니다', '잡지사에서 일하다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: '-사' means company, so a company making newspapers is a '신문사' and one making books is a '출판사'. A company making magazines is a 잡지사. You say '잡지사에 다니다' or '잡지사에서 일하다'.

examples.ko: 후반전에 우리 팀이 한 골을 넣었어요.
examples.en: Our team scored one goal in the second half.
The second half starts in ten minutes.
When the second half came, the players were very tired.
I started watching yesterday's match from the second half.

examples.ko: 전반전에는 지고 있었지만 후반전을 잘 뛰었어요.
examples.en: We were losing in the first half, but we ran well in the second.

examples.ko: 후반전의 마지막 오 분이 가장 떨렸어요.
examples.en: The last five minutes of the second half were the most nerve-racking.

explain: 반대는 '전반전'이에요. 축구처럼 경기를 반으로 나누는 운동에 써요. 야구는 '회', 농구는 보통 '쿼터'로 나눠요. 후반전에도 승부가 안 나면 '연장전'을 해요.
explain_en: The opposite is '전반전'. It is used for sports like soccer that split a match into two halves. Baseball is divided into '회' and basketball usually into '쿼터'. If there is still no winner after the second half, they play '연장전'.

examples.en: We ran out of toilet paper rolls.
I found an old scroll in the drawer.

examples.ko: 선생님이 두루마리에 큰 글씨로 이름을 쓰셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher wrote the name in big letters on the scroll.

examples.ko: 이 두루마리는 한 장씩 뜯어서 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can tear this roll off one sheet at a time.
I rolled the painting into a scroll and brought it.
The roll rolled across the floor, so I quickly picked it up.

explain: 마트에서는 '두루마리 휴지'처럼 말아 놓은 휴지를 부를 때 앞에 붙여요. 한 장씩 뽑아 쓰는 휴지는 '각 티슈'라고 해요. 옛날에 길게 써서 둘둘 말아 둔 종이도 두루마리라고 불러요.
explain_en: For rolled-up tissue you put it in front, as in '두루마리 휴지'. Tissue you pull out one sheet at a time is called '각 티슈'. A long sheet of paper written on and rolled up in the old days is also called 두루마리.

en: both work to earn income (a couple)

examples.ko: 저와 아내는 둘 다 일하니까 맞벌이해요.
examples.en: My wife and I both work, so we are a two-income couple.

examples.ko: 부모님은 오래 맞벌이하셔서 저를 할머니가 키워 주셨어요.
examples.en: My parents both worked for a long time, so my grandmother raised me.
I want us both to keep working even after the baby is born.
Couples who both work share the housework.

examples.ko: 예전에는 맞벌이했지만 지금은 아내가 쉬고 있어요.
examples.en: We both worked before, but now my wife is taking a break.
Housing is expensive, so we have no choice but to both work.

explain: '맞벌이 부부'처럼 명사로도 많이 써요. 반대는 한 사람만 돈을 버는 '외벌이'예요. 주어는 부부나 가족이어서 한 사람이 혼자 '맞벌이해요'라고 하면 어색해요.
explain_en: It also works as a noun, as in '맞벌이 부부'. The opposite is '외벌이', where only one person earns money. The subject is a couple or a family, so one person alone saying '맞벌이해요' sounds odd.

examples.en: A bulldozer is pushing the ground flat at the construction site.

examples.ko: 불도저 소리 때문에 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: I could not sleep because of the bulldozer noise.
The child moved sand with a toy bulldozer.
I saw a big bulldozer up close for the first time.

examples.ko: 산 앞에 불도저도 있고 크레인도 서 있었어요.
examples.en: In front of the mountain there was a bulldozer and a crane too.

examples.ko: 이 불도저에는 앞에 큰 삽이 달려 있어요.
examples.en: This bulldozer has a big blade on the front.

explain: 앞에 넓은 판이 달려 흙을 밀어내는 기계예요. 땅을 파는 기계는 '포클레인'이라고 부르는 경우가 많고, 정식 이름은 '굴착기'예요. 사람에게 쓰면 한번 마음먹으면 막힘없이 밀고 나가는 모습을 말해요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 다른 의견을 듣지 않고 힘차게 일을 진행할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a person drives a job forward forcefully without listening to other opinions.

explain_en: It has a wide blade on the front that pushes soil. The machine that digs the ground is often called '포클레인', and its formal name is '굴착기'. Used about a person, it describes someone who pushes ahead without stopping once they decide.

examples.en: My friend's handwriting style is really pretty.

examples.ko: 이 글씨체가 읽기 편해서 계속 써요.
examples.en: I keep using this lettering style because it is easy to read.
I looked at my teacher's handwriting and copied it.
The mood changes depending on the lettering style.

examples.ko: 손으로 쓴 것 같은 글씨체로 카드를 꾸몄어요.
examples.en: I decorated the card in a hand-written looking style.

examples.ko: 글씨체까지 닮은 두 사람이 쌍둥이 같아요.
examples.en: The two people look like twins, even down to their handwriting.

explain: '글씨가 예뻐요'는 쓴 솜씨를 칭찬하는 말이고, '글씨체가 예뻐요'는 글자 모양의 스타일을 말해요. 컴퓨터에서는 '글꼴'이나 '폰트'라고 해요.
explain_en: '글씨가 예뻐요' praises how well someone writes, while '글씨체가 예뻐요' talks about the style of the letter shapes. On a computer people say '글꼴' or '폰트'.

examples.en: This song has really beautiful lyrics.
We memorized the lyrics and sang together.
I heard the singer wrote the lyrics herself.
I looked up the words in the lyrics in the dictionary.
I like both the lyrics and the melody.
To study Korean, I learn words through song lyrics.

explain: '가사'와 같은 뜻으로 써요. 노랫말은 우리말 단어이고 가사는 한자어예요. '가사'는 집안일이라는 뜻도 있어서 헷갈릴 때 '노랫말'이라고 하면 분명해요. '노랫말을 쓰다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It means the same as '가사'. 노랫말 is a native Korean word while '가사' is Sino-Korean. '가사' also means housework, so saying 노랫말 makes it clear. You say '노랫말을 쓰다'.

en: the rest of the story; behind-the-scenes story

examples.en: After the drama ended, I was curious about what happened next.
I read the behind-the-scenes stories from the film set in a book.

examples.ko: 그 사건의 뒷이야기는 아직 아무도 몰라요.
examples.en: Nobody knows the rest of that incident's story yet.

examples.ko: 선생님의 학창 시절 뒷이야기에 모두 귀를 기울였어요.
examples.en: Everyone listened closely to the teacher's stories from her school days.
I know the first part, so please tell me the rest too.
After hearing even the rest of the story, I understood.

explain: '뒷담화'와는 달라요. 뒷담화는 없는 사람의 흉을 보는 일이고, 뒷이야기는 어떤 일이 끝난 뒤의 이야기나 알려지지 않은 사정이에요. 영화나 방송에서는 '비하인드 스토리'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is different from '뒷담화'. 뒷담화 is speaking badly about someone who is not there, while 뒷이야기 is what comes after something ends, or little-known circumstances behind it. For movies and TV people also say '비하인드 스토리'.

examples.en: I had a headache, so I took an aspirin.

examples.ko: 이 약은 아스피린이 아니라 다른 약이에요.
examples.en: This medicine is not aspirin but a different one.
I bought a bottle of aspirin at the pharmacy.
There is aspirin in my backpack, but no bandage.
The first aid kit has aspirin in it too.
Some people are allergic to aspirin.

explain: '진통제'는 아픔을 줄이는 약을 두루 부르는 이름이고, 아스피린은 그중 하나의 약 이름이에요. 약은 '먹다'와 같이 쓰고, 어른께는 '드시다'라고 해요. 병원에서 받는 약은 '처방약'이라고 해요.
explain_en: '진통제' is the general name for medicine that reduces pain, and 아스피린 is one specific medicine among them. Medicine goes with '먹다', and for an elder you say '드시다'. Medicine from a hospital prescription is '처방약'.

examples.ko: 아이가 앞니가 빠져서 웃을 때 귀여워요.
examples.en: The child lost a front tooth, and looks cute when smiling.

examples.ko: 앞니로 사과를 한 입 베어 물었어요.
examples.en: I took a bite of the apple with my front teeth.
I looked in the mirror and brushed my front teeth carefully.
There is red pepper powder stuck on your front tooth.

examples.ko: 앞니는 음식을 자르고 어금니는 잘게 갈아요.
examples.en: Front teeth cut food and molars grind it up finely.
The baby got front teeth and started taking first steps too.

explain: 글자는 '앞니'지만 소리는 [암니]로 들려요. 안쪽의 이는 '어금니'라고 해요. '이를 닦다', '이가 빠지다'처럼 '이'만 써도 되고 '앞니'는 어느 이인지 말할 때 써요.
explain_en: It is written 앞니 but sounds like [암니]. The teeth further back are '어금니'. You can just say '이' as in '이를 닦다' or '이가 빠지다', and use 앞니 when you need to say which tooth.

examples.en: Seoul is a city with a very large population.
I surveyed the city's population and put it in a table.

examples.ko: 이 마을의 인구수는 해마다 줄고 있어요.
examples.en: This village's population is getting smaller every year.

examples.ko: 인구수에 맞게 학교를 더 지어야 해요.
examples.en: We need to build more schools to match the population.
Please compare the population and the area together.
In terms of population, Busan comes after Seoul.

explain: '인구가 많아요'처럼 '인구'만 써도 같은 뜻이에요. 인구수는 사람 수를 숫자로 말할 때 어울려요. 사람은 '명'으로 세서 '인구 백만 명'이라고 해요.
explain_en: You can say just '인구' as in '인구가 많아요' with the same meaning. 인구수 fits when you talk about the number itself. People are counted with '명', as in '인구 백만 명'.

examples.en: My eldest brother is ten years older than me.

examples.ko: 큰형이 회사에 다닌 지 오 년이 됐어요.
examples.en: It has been five years since my eldest brother started working at a company.
When I was little, I learned Hangeul from my eldest brother.
On holidays the family gathers at my eldest brother's house.
I take after my eldest brother, so I am tall.
My eldest brother and I have similar hobbies.

explain: 남자가 자기 형을 부르는 말이 '형'이고, 여자는 '오빠'라고 해요. 형이 둘 이상이면 가장 위를 '큰형', 그다음은 '둘째 형'이라고 해요. 직접 부를 때는 보통 그냥 '형'이라고 불러요.
explain_en: A man calls his older brother '형', while a woman says '오빠'. With two or more older brothers, the eldest is 큰형 and the next is '둘째 형'. When calling him directly, people usually just say '형'.

examples.en: I steamed a kabocha squash and ate it as a snack.
I peeled the skin to make kabocha soup.
This kabocha is sweet and soft.
Kabocha was on sale at the mart, so I bought one.
I boiled kabocha and potatoes together.
You can also make a cake with kabocha.

explain: '애호박'은 연한 초록색이어서 찌개나 전에 넣고, 단호박은 껍질이 단단하고 속이 노랗고 달아요. 그냥 '호박'은 이 둘을 포함해 여러 호박을 부르는 말이에요. '단'은 '달다'에서 온 말이에요.
explain_en: '애호박' is pale green and goes into stews and pancakes, while 단호박 has a hard skin and a sweet yellow inside. Plain '호박' is the name covering both and other kinds. The '단' comes from '달다' (sweet).

examples.en: I washed my face and brushed my teeth in the hotel bathroom.
I need to wash up, so please get a towel ready.

examples.ko: 세면할 때 쓰는 물이 따뜻하면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I hope the water for washing my face is warm.

examples.ko: 여행 중에는 세면하기가 불편할 때가 있어요.
examples.en: Washing up can be inconvenient when you travel.
Please put on lotion after you wash your face.
I washed my face with cold water and woke up.

explain: '세면대', '세면도구'처럼 다른 말에 들어가는 경우가 있어요. 말할 때 얼굴을 씻는 일은 보통 '세수하다'라고 해요. 세면하다는 글이나 안내문에서 더 딱딱한 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It appears inside other words such as '세면대' (washbasin) and '세면도구' (toiletries). In speech, washing your face is usually '세수하다'. 세면하다 sounds stiffer, like written notices.

examples.en: My father bought a new car this month.
The color of this new car is really cool.
When a new car comes out, pictures are posted online.
Many reporters gathered at the new car launch event.
Many people buy used cars rather than new ones.

examples.ko: 회사 앞에 신차로 보이는 하얀 차가 서 있어요.
examples.en: A white car that looks brand new is parked in front of the office.

explain: 반대는 '중고차'예요. 친구와 이야기할 때는 '새 차'라고 하는 경우가 많고, 신차는 '신차 출시', '신차 발표'처럼 뉴스나 광고에 어울려요. '신제품'의 '신'도 같은 글자예요.
explain_en: The opposite is '중고차'. Talking with a friend, people often say '새 차', while 신차 fits news and ads, as in '신차 출시' and '신차 발표'. The '신' is the same character as in '신제품'.

examples.en: When we first meet, we say a greeting like 'Hello'.

examples.ko: 선생님이 쓰신 카드 인사말이 정말 따뜻했어요.
examples.en: The greeting in the card my teacher wrote was really warm.

examples.ko: 이 인사말은 아침에도 저녁에도 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can use this greeting in the morning and in the evening.
Putting a name in the greeting feels friendlier.
At the wedding my father gave a short greeting speech too.
Just memorizing greetings in a foreign language makes travel fun.

explain: '인사'는 고개를 숙이거나 말로 하는 행동 전체를, 인사말은 그때 입으로 하는 말만 가리켜요. 행동은 '인사하다', 말은 '인사말을 하다'라고 해요. 윗사람에게는 '인사드리다'라고 해요.
explain_en: '인사' covers the whole action of bowing or greeting, while 인사말 is only the words you say. The action is '인사하다' and the words are '인사말을 하다'. To someone older you say '인사드리다'.

examples.en: I feel deep respect for my parents.
My respect toward my teacher grew little by little.

examples.ko: 존경심은 말보다 행동으로 보여 줘야 해요.
examples.en: You should show respect through actions rather than words.

examples.ko: 그는 존경심으로 가득한 눈으로 할아버지를 바라봤어요.
examples.en: He looked at his grandfather with eyes full of respect.
It was a small action that came from respect.
It is behavior with neither respect nor manners.

explain: '호기심', '애국심'처럼 '-심'은 마음을 나타내요. '존경심을 느끼다', '존경심을 갖다'처럼 써요. 사람을 대할 때는 '선생님을 존경해요'라고 동사로 말하고, 다른 사람의 의견이나 선택을 인정할 때는 '존중'을 써요.
explain_en: As in '호기심' and '애국심', the '-심' part shows a feeling in the mind. It goes with '존경심을 느끼다' and '존경심을 갖다'. About a person you can use the verb, as in '선생님을 존경해요', and for accepting someone's opinion or choice you use '존중'.

examples.en: My grandfather played the harmonica for me.
This harmonica is small, so it fits in a pocket.
I tried playing an easy children's song on the harmonica.
I heard a harmonica sound and looked out the window.
I do not know where the harmonica went.
I want to learn both the harmonica and the guitar.

explain: 입으로 불어서 소리를 내므로 '하모니카를 불다'라고 해요. 악기마다 동사가 달라서 피아노와 기타는 '치다', 바이올린은 '켜다'라고 해요. '연주하다'는 모든 악기에 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: You make the sound by blowing, so you say '하모니카를 불다'. The verb changes by instrument: '치다' for piano and guitar, '켜다' for violin. '연주하다' works for any instrument.

examples.en: In autumn I picked apples at an orchard.
My grandfather runs a small orchard.
Pear trees stand in rows in the orchard.

examples.ko: 과수원 주인이 갓 딴 복숭아를 주셨어요.
examples.en: The orchard owner gave me peaches just picked.
In spring the orchard is full of white flowers.
We went on a field trip to an orchard.

explain: 채소를 키우는 곳은 '밭', 쌀을 키우는 곳은 '논', 과일나무를 키우는 곳은 과수원이에요. 일하는 사람은 '과수원을 하다', 과일을 따는 일은 '따다'와 같이 써요.
explain_en: A place for vegetables is a '밭', for rice a '논', and for fruit trees a 과수원. The owner says '과수원을 하다' (run an orchard), and picking fruit uses '따다'.

examples.en: Rabbits have long hind legs, so they jump well.

examples.ko: 강아지가 뒷다리로 서서 간식을 달라고 했어요.
examples.en: The puppy stood on its hind legs and asked for a snack.
The back legs of the chair are weak, so you must be careful.
The cat hurt its hind leg and went to the animal hospital.

examples.ko: 말은 뒷다리에 힘을 주고 높이 뛰어올랐어요.
examples.en: The horse put strength into its hind legs and jumped high.
It is an animal whose front legs and hind legs are both strong.

explain: 반대는 '앞다리'예요. 다리가 네 개인 동물에 쓰고, 의자나 책상 같은 물건의 뒤쪽 다리에도 써요. 사람의 다리는 '앞'과 '뒤'로 나누지 않고 그냥 '다리'라고 해요.
explain_en: The opposite is '앞다리'. It is used for four-legged animals, and also for the back legs of things like chairs or desks. A person's legs are not split into front and back; they are just '다리'.

examples.en: My younger sister became a middle school girl this year.

examples.ko: 버스에서 여중생 두 명이 웃고 있었어요.
examples.en: Two middle school girls were laughing on the bus.
That middle school girl is very good at running.
The middle school girls lined up in their uniforms.
My teacher does the work of teaching middle school girls.

examples.ko: 여중생에게 인기 있는 책을 추천해 주세요.
examples.en: Please recommend a book that is popular with middle school girls.

explain: '여자 중학생'을 줄인 말이에요. '여-'는 여자라는 뜻이라서 '여고생', '여대생'도 같은 방식이에요. 남자는 '남중생'이라고도 하고, 성별을 따지지 않으면 '중학생'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a shortened form of '여자 중학생'. The '여-' means female, so '여고생' and '여대생' work the same way. For boys people also say '남중생', and if gender does not matter, '중학생'.

examples.en: Yukhoe is raw meat, so it has to be fresh.
At the restaurant I ordered yukhoe and bibimbap.

examples.ko: 육회에 배와 계란 노른자를 올려 먹어요.
examples.en: We eat yukhoe topped with pear and egg yolk.

examples.ko: 저는 육회를 처음 먹어 봤는데 맛있었어요.
examples.en: It was my first time eating yukhoe and it was tasty.
I was worried whether I would like yukhoe, but it was fine.
I like yukhoe and raw fish too.

explain: '육'은 고기, '회'는 익히지 않은 음식을 부르는 글자예요. 보통 소고기를 양념해서 먹어요. 생선을 날것으로 먹는 음식은 '생선회'예요. '회' 앞에 오는 재료만 달라요.
explain_en: '육' means meat and '회' is food eaten uncooked. It is usually seasoned beef. Raw fish is called '생선회', so the ingredient before '회' changes.

examples.ko: 여름에는 에어컨 때문에 전기세가 많이 나와요.
examples.en: In summer the electricity bill is high because of the air conditioner.

examples.ko: 이번 달 전기세를 아직 못 냈어요.
examples.en: I have not paid this month's electricity bill yet.
The electricity bill is taken out of my account automatically every month.

examples.ko: 전기세 걱정 때문에 난방을 조금만 틀었어요.
examples.en: I worried about the electricity bill, so I used the heating only a little.

examples.ko: 겨울에는 전기세보다 가스비가 더 많이 나와요.
examples.en: In winter the gas bill is higher than the electricity bill.
Both electricity and water bills went up, so living costs are a burden.

explain: '세'는 원래 세금이라는 뜻이지만 일상에서는 '전기세', '수도세'처럼 요금도 이렇게 말해요. 고지서에는 '전기요금'이라고 적혀 있어요. '전기세를 내다', '전기세가 나오다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: '세' originally means tax, but in everyday speech people also call bills this way, as in '전기세' and '수도세'. On the bill itself it is written '전기요금'. It goes with '전기세를 내다' (pay) and '전기세가 나오다' (the bill comes).

examples.en: The autumn leaves turned orange.
I like clothes that have orange in them.

examples.ko: 해가 질 때 하늘이 주황과 분홍으로 물들어요.
examples.en: At sunset the sky is dyed orange and pink.
Orange comes out when you mix red and yellow.
Please paint it a color close to orange.

examples.ko: 주황도 노랑도 밝아서 눈에 잘 띄어요.
examples.en: Both orange and yellow are bright, so they stand out.

explain: '주황색'이라고도 하고 '오렌지색'이라고도 해요. 한자로 '주'는 빨강, '황'은 노랑이어서 빨강과 노랑 사이 색이에요. 과일 오렌지의 색뿐 아니라 감과 귤 색에도 써요.
explain_en: You can say '주황색' or '오렌지색' as well. In the Chinese characters '주' is red and '황' is yellow, so it is the color between red and yellow. It is used not only for the fruit orange but for the color of persimmons and tangerines too.

examples.en: My younger sibling is taller than me.
I share a room with my younger sibling.
I gave my younger sibling a little pocket money.

examples.ko: 친동생은 한 명이고 사촌 동생은 세 명이에요.
examples.en: I have one younger sibling and three younger cousins.
I have a junior I care about like my own younger sibling.
I took my younger sibling all the way to school.

explain: '친'은 피가 같다는 뜻이에요. 사촌 동생이나 친하게 지내는 동생과 나눌 때 써요. 그냥 '동생'이라고 해도 보통은 같은 부모의 동생을 가리켜요.
explain_en: '친' means related by blood. You use it to separate your sibling from a cousin or a friend you call 동생. Just saying '동생' usually also means a younger sibling of the same parents.

examples.en: The factory manager checks the machines every morning.

examples.ko: 우리 공장장은 직원들 이름을 다 알아요.
examples.en: Our factory manager knows the names of all the staff.

examples.ko: 새 공장장이 오고 나서 분위기가 바뀌었어요.
examples.en: After the new factory manager came, the mood changed.
Tell the factory manager about this problem first.

examples.ko: 아버지는 이 년 전부터 공장장으로 일하세요.
examples.en: My father has worked as a factory manager for two years.
The factory manager and the staff had lunch together.

explain: '-장'은 그곳을 책임지는 사람 이름에 붙어요. '팀장', '반장'처럼 써요. 부를 때는 '공장장님'이라고 해요.
explain_en: '-장' marks the person in charge of a place or group, as in '팀장' and '반장'. When addressing the person you say '공장장님'.

examples.ko: 야간 근무자는 밤 열 시에 출근해요.
examples.en: The night shift worker comes to work at ten at night.
We are short of workers, so the work is getting delayed.
I left the key with today's person on duty.
Only people on duty can enter the break room.
The workers greet each other at shift change.
I prepared lunch for all the workers on duty.

explain: '직원'은 그 회사에 속한 사람이고, 근무자는 지금 그 시간이나 장소에서 일하는 사람이에요. '야간 근무자', '당직 근무자'처럼 시간이나 역할 말과 함께 나와요. 아르바이트하는 사람도 근무자라고 부를 수 있어요.
explain_en: A '직원' belongs to the company, while 근무자 is the person working at that time or place. It comes with words for time or role, as in '야간 근무자' and '당직 근무자'. A part-timer can also be called 근무자.

examples.en: I put on mascara to make my eyes look bigger.
I got rained on, so my mascara smudged.

examples.ko: 이 마스카라는 물에 잘 안 지워져요.
examples.en: This mascara does not wash off easily with water.

examples.ko: 가방 안에 마스카라와 립스틱이 들어 있어요.
examples.en: There is mascara and lipstick in my bag.
My eyes sting because of the mascara.
I bought new mascara and lotion too.

explain: 화장품은 보통 '바르다'와 같이 써서 '마스카라를 바르다'라고 해요. 마스카라는 속눈썹에 바르고, 눈 가장자리에 선을 그리는 '아이라인'은 '그리다'를 써요. 지울 때는 '지우다'를 써요.
explain_en: Makeup usually goes with '바르다', so you say '마스카라를 바르다'. Mascara goes on the eyelashes, but drawing a line along the eye, '아이라인', uses '그리다'. To take it off you use '지우다'.

examples.ko: 감기에 걸려서 따뜻한 물에 벌꿀을 넣어 마셨어요.
examples.en: I had a cold, so I drank warm water with honey in it.
This honey has a strong scent and is sweet.
We ran out of honey, so I have to go to the mart.
I spread jam on the bread instead of honey.
I received snacks made with honey as a gift.
I mix honey and lemon to make tea.

explain: 그냥 '꿀'이라고 해도 같은 뜻이에요. 벌이 만든 꿀이라는 점을 분명히 하려고 '벌꿀'이라고 해요. 빵에는 '바르다', 물에는 '타다'를 써서 '물에 꿀을 타다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Just saying '꿀' means the same. 벌꿀 makes clear that it is honey made by bees. For bread you use '바르다', and for stirring it into water '타다', as in '물에 꿀을 타다'.

examples.en: In springtime my nose itches because of pollen.
When springtime comes, there are more people in the mountains.
Spring weather is chilly in the morning and evening.
Every spring we go to see the flowers with my family.
Yellow dust in springtime is not good for your health.
Both spring and fall are good for traveling.

explain: '철'은 한 계절이나 어떤 시기를 뜻해서 '여름철', '장마철', '휴가철'처럼 써요. '봄'은 계절 이름이고, 봄철은 '봄철 건강', '봄철 황사'처럼 봄에 생기는 일과 함께 써요.
explain_en: '철' means a season or a period of the year, as in '여름철', '장마철' and '휴가철'. '봄' is the name of the season, and 봄철 goes with things that happen in spring, like '봄철 건강' and '봄철 황사'.

examples.ko: 이 공장의 생산품은 외국으로 많이 팔려요.
examples.en: This factory's products are sold a lot overseas.
We sell our village's products at the market.

examples.ko: 생산품에 문제가 있으면 바로 알려 주세요.
examples.en: If there is a problem with the product, please tell us right away.

examples.ko: 이 생산품이 어느 나라에서 만들어졌는지 확인해요.
examples.en: I check which country this product was made in.
We made a gift set out of the products.
I compared the prices of our own products and imported products.

explain: '제품'은 만들어 낸 물건 전체를, '상품'은 팔려고 내놓은 물건을 말해요. 생산품은 어느 곳에서 만든 물건이라는 점을 말할 때 써요. 외국에서 들여온 물건은 '수입품'이라고 해요.
explain_en: '제품' is any manufactured item and '상품' is an item put out for sale. 생산품 is used to say an item was made at a certain place. Goods brought in from abroad are '수입품'.

examples.en: In autumn the leaves on the trees turn yellow.
When the wind blew, the leaves shook.

examples.ko: 큰 잎사귀 하나를 주워서 책에 끼웠어요.
examples.en: I picked up one big leaf and put it in a book.
Morning dew has formed on the leaf.

examples.ko: 이 화분은 잎사귀는 크지만 꽃은 작아요.
examples.en: This pot has big leaves but small flowers.
The rabbit ate the leaves happily.

explain: '잎'과 같은 뜻으로 써요. 나무에 달린 잎은 '나뭇잎', 풀의 잎은 '풀잎'이라고도 해요. 떨어진 잎은 '낙엽'이라고 하고, 잎사귀는 잎 하나하나를 말하는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It means the same as '잎'. A leaf on a tree is a '나뭇잎' and a leaf of grass is a '풀잎'. A fallen leaf is a '낙엽', and 잎사귀 has the feel of one leaf at a time.

examples.en: The children folded a crane out of paper.
I go to a paper folding class every weekend.
Doing paper folding works as practice for your hands.

examples.ko: 종이접기는 색종이 한 장만 있으면 시작할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can start paper folding with just one sheet of colored paper.
I borrowed a book about paper folding from the library.

examples.ko: 동생은 종이접기도 잘하고 그림도 잘 그려요.
examples.en: My younger sibling is good at paper folding and drawing too.

explain: '종이를 접다'에서 나온 말이라서 '종이접기를 하다'라고 해요. 접는 종이는 보통 '색종이'를 많이 써요. 접어서 만든 것은 '학', '종이배'처럼 이름을 따로 불러요.
explain_en: It comes from '종이를 접다', so you say '종이접기를 하다'. The paper used is often '색종이' (colored paper). What you make is called by its own name, such as '학' (crane) or '종이배' (paper boat).

examples.en: My older brother plays the clarinet in the school band.
I like the clarinet because its sound is soft.
A clarinet makes sound when you blow into it with your mouth.
The new clarinet arrived, and I started practicing.
I tried playing movie music on the clarinet.

examples.ko: 클라리넷도 불고 피아노도 칠 줄 아는 친구가 있어요.
examples.en: I have a friend who can play both the clarinet and the piano.

explain: 입으로 불어서 소리를 내는 악기라 '클라리넷을 불다'라고 해요. 피아노나 기타는 '치다', 바이올린은 '켜다'를 써요. 외래어 표기는 '클라리네트'가 아니라 '클라리넷'이에요.
explain_en: You make the sound by blowing, so you say '클라리넷을 불다'. For piano and guitar you use '치다' and for violin '켜다'. The standard spelling is 클라리넷, not '클라리네트'.

examples.en: '책방' and '서점' are synonyms.

examples.ko: 사전에서 동의어를 찾아서 글을 바꿔 썼어요.
examples.en: I found synonyms in the dictionary and rewrote my text.

examples.ko: 한 단어에 동의어가 여러 개 있기도 해요.
examples.en: One word can have several synonyms.

examples.ko: 동의어는 서로 바꿔 쓸 수 있지만 느낌이 조금 달라요.
examples.en: Synonyms can replace each other, but the feeling is a little different.

examples.ko: 이 단어의 동의어에는 어떤 것이 있어요?
examples.en: What synonyms does this word have?

examples.ko: 동의어와 반의어를 함께 공부하면 단어가 쉽게 외워져요.
examples.en: If you study synonyms and antonyms together, words are easier to memorize.

explain: 뜻이 같은 말은 동의어, 뜻이 비슷한 말은 '유의어', 뜻이 반대인 말은 '반의어'라고 해요. 한자 '同'은 같다는 뜻이에요. 사전에서는 '비슷한말'이라는 이름으로 나오기도 해요.
explain_en: Words with the same meaning are 동의어, words with similar meaning are '유의어', and words with opposite meaning are '반의어'. The character '同' means same. In dictionaries you may also see it listed as '비슷한말'.

examples.en: I ran through the rain all the way to school.
I waited a long time in the rain without an umbrella.
The city in the rain looks quiet and lonely.

examples.ko: 빗속으로 걸어 나가는 뒷모습이 슬퍼 보였어요.
examples.en: The figure walking out into the rain looked sad.
Even in the rain, people stood in line and waited.

examples.ko: 그는 빗속에 서서 아무 말도 하지 않았어요.
examples.en: He stood in the rain and said nothing.

explain: '물속', '꿈속', '마음속'처럼 '-속'이 붙은 말이에요. '빗속을 걷다', '빗속에서 기다리다'처럼 비를 맞는 상황에서 써요. 사이시옷(ㅅ)이 들어가서 '비속'이 아니라 '빗속'이라고 써요.
explain_en: It is built like '물속', '꿈속' and '마음속', with '-속' attached. It is used in situations where you are out in the rain, as in '빗속을 걷다' and '빗속에서 기다리다'. A sound-linking ㅅ is added, so it is written 빗속, not '비속'.
